intended_object: The canonical K-algebra map K[GL_n]/(det − 1) = K[x_ij][det⁻¹]/(det − 1) → K[x_ij]/(det − 1) between the two presentations of the coordinate ring of SL_n. It sends each x_ij to x_ij and is the inverse of the obvious map in the other direction. This is inferred from the docstring and from the theorems after it, which show that the two maps are mutually inverse.
explanation:
The localized general linear coordinate ring K[x_ij][det⁻¹] maps to K[x_ij]/(det − 1). This map, `localizationToPolynomialQuotient`, comes from the universal property of the localization, which applies because det maps to 1, a unit. The definition lifts this map through the quotient by the ideal (det − 1). The proof that the ideal is killed is correct: det goes to 1, so every multiple of det − 1 goes to 0. This is exactly the standard canonical map. The theorems that follow show it is a two-sided inverse of `polynomialQuotientToCoordinateRing`, which confirms it is the intended isomorphism.

The setting is already general: any commutative ring K and any finite index type with decidable equality. Mathlib has no SL_n coordinate ring, so there is no counterpart. One might call this map half of an equivalence, a technical device, but it is a genuine canonical algebra homomorphism, and it is defined correctly.
